institutionName: Norwegian University of Science and Technology (NTNU)

questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I looked for a city that would be close to nature, but still well connected and that had good student-opportunities. I was also looking for a university that had some of the course I thought of taking in Copenhagen.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was quite easy, there were some meetings designed for exchange students, and we also got most of the information by email.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We didn't receive any personal assistance per say. But we did attend a lot of different meetings and different welcome-to-Trondheim events that provide the needed assistance to get around town and figure out how the university works compared to UCPH.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
I lived in one of the "Studentby". It started out being quite complicated to try and find some housing. You should do so by looking at the
hybel.no
website. We found some rooms with a shared kitchen in one of the many studentby in Trondheim.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It was a fine place and it was well connected to the city centre and campus, even though it was a bit further away.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The studentby in itself wasn't super nice (not really hyggeligt), but it worked fine.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: We didn't really have to do anything. Most of course I wanted to attend were free of charge and had no limitations, so it was nice and easy to sign up.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You had to sign up for the class and the exam on a website called Studentweb. It was also possible to sign up/switch classes after you had signed up, until a specific date.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: If in need, you could talk with a studivejleder.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all of the classes that I wanted to attend.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: You will probably not end up with the exact list of classes that you decided upon at home. Take your time during the first month to find the ones that you think are interesting and also offer a good teaching schedule.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was quite different from UCPH.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Most of my classes were of Intermediate level II.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: NTNU only offers lectures - there is no aftermath during a group-classs-project or teaching in smaller groups. You will have to do a lot of self-studying.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Immunology - Condensed Introduction to Neuroscience - Medical Molecular Bacteriology - Psychological Disorders.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I liked all of my courses, but most of all Immunology. The course was very fulfilled and it seemed a bit harder than the other courses that I had. 
The condensed introduction to Neuroscience class was actually online, which I though was a bit of a shame. But it was still quite interesting and the book that they advice is very good. 
The Molecular Medical Bacteriology was a bit confusing. We also had to do a bioinformatics exercise, which I didn't quite understand - but mostly because we did it on a platform that no students really knew how to use. The class focuses on sequencing methods and their use in the diagnosis of presence of bacteria. 
The psychological disorders course was in Norwegian, which was fine to understand. I though it was really interesting and I picked it even though it is not entirely related to my BA degree. I chose the course out of pure interest.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Some things were more expensive than in Denmark, but most of it is very similar. I went on a few more small trips than I at first had anticipated. But I'm very grateful that I did.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Housing was a bit more expensive than expected. This was mostly because the rent becomes higher when you are only staying for 6 months. Most people only offer 1 year contracts.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The sports facilities are great!!!

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: All sorts of activities are avalaible through the NTNUI (NTNU Idræt), the ESN (Erasmus Student Network) and a lot of other smaller clubs such as the Surfing-club, the Ski-club etc.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Go on trips!!! And sign-up for some gym classes with your friends!.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go on a hike with some of your new friends :)

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was very easy (mostly because Denmark and Norway are quite similar).

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I unfortunately did not meet that many local students...

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The currency of the norwegian crown being higher than the danish crown.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: All Norwegian people seem to be sports-enthusiast that spend their free time in the outdoors.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Look at the course catalogue before hand, find some friends (show up at the introduction parties and welcome committees), and enjoy the nature!!!! And sign up for NTNUI it really gives you a great deal of opportunities for all kinds of sports!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I do not think so.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer:
Meeting such great people in another country. 
Learning a different way of attending university and studying, than what I have been used to. 
I really really enjoyed being able to spend so much time outdoors and enjoying the beautiful nature of Norway. Put the "ja-hat" on!

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Having to navigate in school studies, but also spending time with friends, experiencing new things everyday, keeping up with your sports, going on trips and calling home.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: No further comments

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
